title: Altered neuronal start codon stringency favors cap-independent repeat-associated non-AUG translation.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the full Europe PMC supplement (4.48 MB): it contains 12 article figure images plus one 13-page PDF. I extracted the PDF text page by page: pages 2-8 are figure legends for Supplementary Figures S1-S7, pages 9-13 are Supplementary Table S1, which is a list of reporter plasmid DNA sequences. There is no spreadsheet, CSV or any numeric source-data file anywhere in the supplement, and the data availability statement says only 'All study data are available in the article and/or the supplementary information'.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Sample sizes per condition (n = 12, 9, 6 or 3 wells), the cell types used (HEK293, HeLa, rat primary hippocampal neurons, human induced neurons and astrocytes), and the re-analysis of Allen Brain Atlas single-nucleus RNA sequencing (226 neuronal and 6 astrocyte transcriptomic clusters) all come from the text and figure legends; I could not check any underlying numbers because none were deposited.

a1_downloadable.note: The supplement downloads, but it holds no data: 13 PDF pages of figure legends plus a table of plasmid sequences. Every measurement in the paper exists only as a bar chart in a figure image; no numeric file, no repository accession, no GitHub or Zenodo deposit.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The thing to predict (luminescence-based translation efficiency of each reporter) is not a column anywhere. It would have to be constructed by digitising bar heights off figure images, which is exactly the 'construct the label' failure.

a3_inputs_present.note: Reporter DNA sequences are genuinely present in Supplementary Table S1 (I read them in the PDF), so the model input side would be fine if labels existed.

a4_units_stated.note: Legends state the normalisation clearly: nanoluciferase signal divided by firefly signal, expressed relative to the AUG reporter or to GA70. Not assessed further given A1/A2 failure.

a5_enough_rows.note: Counting from the legends, the whole study is roughly 30-60 distinct reporter-by-cell-type-by-treatment conditions at n = 3-12 wells each, i.e. a few hundred wells and only tens of unique constructs. Far below the ~1,500-row bar, and I could verify no row count because no table exists.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small, but there is nothing to load.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked at all: there is no download whose counts could be compared with the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels are real physical measurements (luciferase luminescence from transfected cells), not another model's output, so provenance is clean in principle. Irrelevant given the data is not released.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the paper releases no measurement table, so nothing can be trained or tested.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use messenger RNA sequence around a start site to predict how much protein a cell makes from it.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered would train on reporter messenger RNA sequences (the 5' leader, the start codon and its surrounding context, and the repeat tract) paired with a measured translation output, for maybe 30-60 distinct constructs here, which is far too few.
plain_idea.predict: Translation efficiency, measured as nanoluciferase light output divided by a co-transfected firefly luciferase control, read on a plate reader 24 hours after transfecting the messenger RNA into cells.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups working on repeat expansion diseases such as C9orf72 amyotrophic lateral sclerosis would want to know which near-AUG start codons fire in neurons; but this paper's numbers are only in bar charts, so nothing can be learned from it computationally.

ml_idea: Predicting cell-type-specific start codon usage and translation efficiency from 5' leader sequence is a genuinely interesting task for a nucleotide language model, but it needs a large-scale measurement set (a massively parallel reporter assay with thousands of leader variants, e.g. published 5' UTR MPRA libraries), not this paper's few dozen hand-built reporters.

effort.compute_note: Only the 4.48 MB supplement zip was handled; no modelling workload was estimated because no dataset exists.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open the supplement and look for a single numeric file. Took five minutes: there is none, only figure legends and plasmid sequences.

verdict_reason: A classic small-scale experimental cell-biology paper with no deposited data. The entire supplement is a 13-page PDF of figure legends plus reporter plasmid sequences; every translation measurement lives only inside bar-chart images, so A1 (nothing downloadable to model), A2 (label would have to be digitised from figures) and A5 (tens of constructs, not thousands) all fail. The underlying biological question - which near-AUG start codons initiate translation in neurons - is a good machine-learning question, but it needs a massively parallel reporter dataset, not this one.
